answer: Section 2 identifies the two essential components of Double/Debiased Machine Learning as **Neyman orthogonality** and **cross-fitting**. [19cea224507fdb1853fa43fc456ece5c | page 9]

The target parameter \(\theta_0\) is a low-dimensional object of interest, such as an average treatment effect or a fixed vector of regression coefficients. It is often defined as the solution to a moment condition, \(E[m(W;\theta_0,\eta_0)]=0\). [3fc918bfa4346bbf4d5a72f77e0f146a | page 9] [1bb190e771af1499aa40fa479e948ffb | page 3]

Neyman orthogonality makes the estimator less sensitive to nuisance-parameter estimation errors: small deviations from the true nuisance value do not change the moment function to first order. [90c3b5213c632d1e7a0b1b069959fc95 | page 16]
Cross-fitting is intended to reduce the dependence between first-step estimation error and the data used to estimate the target parameter. [46b3d3c66f0f888a2ab9bfced5cddb51 | page 20]

A one-time split leaves some observations out of nuisance estimation and others out of target-parameter estimation, so each step uses only a subset of the data. Cross-fitting rotates the folds: each fold is used in turn to estimate the target while the other folds estimate the nuisance parameters. Thus, across rotations, all observations contribute to both steps, avoiding the efficiency loss of using only a subset for either task. [a1b3a5c7ca75cea978cdfddf08d10a18 | page 20] [46b3d3c66f0f888a2ab9bfced5cddb51 | page 20]
The DML estimator combines Neyman orthogonal scores with cross-fitting. [0394cbc044adaf0319490b78f7cfa5e6 | page 22]
With Neyman-orthogonal scores and cross-fitting, standard errors for the DML estimator can be computed as if the nuisance functions were known. [00179456a14aa5a51f9f6f107ae6ec73 | page 22]

Because the IV comparison uses Neyman-orthogonal scores for each approach, the authors treat regularization bias as controlled for and interpret differences as the effect of overfitting and cross-fitting. A fold-specific nuisance estimate is fit using a different fold from the one held out for evaluating the score. Since the observations are independent, the training-fold data used to construct the estimate are independent of the held-out observations; sample splitting therefore mimics estimating the nuisance function on one independent dataset and evaluating it on another.
